doc: Identifier kinds. A prefix is display and lookup syntax only: stores keep the canonical value (a UUID, a trace id or a provider token) and the reader adds or strips the prefix. A full handle is <prefix>_<canonical without dashes>; a short handle is <prefix>_<4 to 31 leading hex characters> and is only meaningful inside a scope.

kinds.doc: The customer account.
A durable room with zero or more Episodes over time.
One live occurrence inside a Space.
A person's or agent's seat in one Episode. generation counts its joins; the person across Episodes is the User or Agent.
The tenant's identifier for a person, carried across Episodes.
The tenant's identifier for an AI agent, carried across Episodes.
A persistent install or browser profile. device_ephemeral is true when storage was unavailable and the id lives only for this client session.
One SDK client object's lifetime. Owns seq. The CHK- diagnostic code is derived from it.

kinds.authority: minted at the user action that starts it
kinds.doc: One user-visible attempt, such as a join, spanning many requests and traces. Never an alias for a trace.

kinds.authority: minted per attempt by the receiving server
kinds.doc: One request attempt. A retry is a new request in the same journey.
A W3C trace. A journey links to one or more traces.
A W3C span.
Chalk's record of one media transport. The provider's id sits beside it as provider_media_id.
The media provider's session id. Called a session by the provider; it is not a client session.
One Sync websocket.
One kernel op. parent_op_id links nested ops.
One authoritative server decision.
A recording of an Episode.
A background job. attempt counts its runs.
One webhook delivery to a tenant.
A request to be admitted to an Episode.
One telemetry record. Delivery semantics belong to contract C3.
One delivered batch of records. Delivery semantics belong to contract C3.
One checker finding.
One flags snapshot: the hash of the canonical flag map a record ran under. The obs.flags_snapshot fact holds the map itself.

kinds.authority: the API, when it issues the upload
kinds.doc: One diagnostic bundle a client uploaded after a problem report or a live request (slice 13).
A tenant API key, by its row id. The secret and its hash are credentials: never logged.
A tenant's webhook endpoint. Each delivery to it is a whd_.

session_meanings.doc: The dashboard calls an Episode a session. Read session:<id> there as an Episode.
The media provider's session, stored as provider_media_id.
The dashboard's signed-in session (SessionDTO). It is a credential: never logged, never looked up.

diagnostic_code.doc: A code a person can read aloud from their screen. It is four Crockford base32 characters from the first 20 bits of the client session id. It is a scoped lookup, never an authority: it matches roughly one client session in a million, so the reader scopes it by tenant and time and returns every candidate.
